status: pre-registered: written and to be committed before any replay baseline or candidate experiment is run on v2a or v2b
label: the timelines are trajectory-derived (estimated from stop-line crossings; no signal head or controller log was read); every result read under this design is simulated
purpose: The real junction (NGSIM Lankershim intersection 2, 2005-06-16 08:30-08:45 PDT) has no signal log, so its timeline is estimated, and the estimate has choices the evidence does not settle. A candidate's verdict changed sign between the two committed versions (I1 mean delay +5.40 s [5.13, 5.67] on version 1, -0.75 s [-0.90, -0.60] on version 2), and seed intervals do not carry timeline uncertainty. The ensemble replays the same observed vehicles under every defensible timeline and reports a verdict only where it holds on all of them; otherwise it reports the disagreement.

inputs.estimator: cairoflow_perception.ngsim_junction.estimate_signal_timeline with the scenario record's SignalPolicy; members differ only in the two SignalRevision flags
inputs.candidates: the three outcomes the validator accepted on 2026-10-28 (experiments/runs/ngsim-int2-experiment-20261028T084336Z outcomes.json, hash-checked against its report.json): I1, I2, I3. Each was validated on the cut cycle and is mapped onto a replay by phase identity (cairoflow_simulation.replay_candidates). No new candidate is generated and no model is called.

members.rationale: The scenario record's timeline (ADR-019), unchanged. Permissive left turners count only where an arm's throughs are too few, because they also cross at the end of green; each yellow ends just after the last crossing, so greens are lower bounds.
members.evidence: West green in the window 68 s; all heads red for 111 s of [118, 751) (including two 1 s clearances), 32 s of it at 211-243 s while west lefts crossed; west lefts 6 of 23 and west throughs 1 of 30 shown red.

members.rationale: Version 2 (ADR-023, DATA_REGISTER.md §22), unchanged. An arm with no left head counts its permissive lefts as green evidence (they move only on that green); each yellow starts at the last crossing, so every reference vehicle crosses in green.
members.evidence: West green in the window 114 s; all heads red for 49 s; no west left or west through shown red.

members.rationale: The permissive-left rule of version 2 with the yellow placement of version 1: restores the west greens served only by permissive lefts, without lengthening any green past its last crossing.
members.evidence: West green in the window 91 s; all heads red for 84 s; no west left or west through shown red; north and south greens as version 1.

members.rationale: The yellow placement of version 2 with the permissive-left rule of version 1: every green runs to its last crossing, but greens served only by permissive lefts stay out.
members.evidence: West green in the window 84 s; all heads red for 83 s; west lefts 5 of 23 and west throughs 1 of 30 shown red; north and south greens as version 2.

why_all_four_are_required: Neither axis is settled by the evidence, and each setting is a bound rather than the truth. Permissive lefts: off drops greens in which only lefts crossed (west lefts crossed while version 1 shows every head red); on lengthens greens by lefts that sneak through at their end. Yellow: at the end, the last vehicle crosses at the very end of yellow; at the start, nobody uses the yellow; the truth lies between. The axes interact: the west green in the window is 68, 91, 84 and 114 s on T1-T4, so adding the two separate effects (107 s) misses version 2 by 7 s. The west green is what I1 and I3 cut, and T3 and T4 lie between the two versions on which I1's delay verdict changes sign.

replay.same_frame_note: Every member replays the same 731 observed vehicles over the same window with the same seeds and settings. Cross-street entries are anchored to each member's own greens (trace_demand), so each member is a self-consistent reconstruction.

admissibility_gate.G1: Provenance: the timeline is derived by estimate_signal_timeline from the committed world model and policy with only the two SignalRevision flags changed, and the same run reproduces the committed version 1 (signal_timeline.json) and version 2 (signal_timeline_v2.json) byte for byte, or nothing is written.
admissibility_gate.G2: No conflicting heads: no second in which two conflicting heads (cairoflow_perception.ngsim_junction.heads_conflict) both show green or yellow, and no phase of the compiled replay program giving priority green to two foe links (the validator's check 7 applied to the replay program).
admissibility_gate.G3: Same frame: the known window equals version 1's, [118, 751) s, so the same observed vehicles are replayed; the cut cycle at 564 s compiles (it drives the drain); the compiled replay program shows the timeline second by second (0 seconds differing).
admissibility_gate.G4: No worse than version 1 on the evidence: in [118, 751), no through or left movement has more of its observed stop-line crossings shown red than on version 1 (right turns excluded: right turn on red is legal and modelled).
admissibility_gate.G5: A valid replay baseline: valid on all 20 pre-registered seeds, with 0 teleports, 0 collisions, every vehicle inserted and arrived, and reruns identical.
admissibility_gate.where_checked: G1, G2 (timeline), G3 (window and cut) and G4 by scripts/build_ngsim_int2_timeline_ensemble.py; G2 (program) and G3 (window, program) by scripts/build_ngsim_int2_realism.py before any run; G5 by the baseline build; all five again by scripts/run_ngsim_int2_timeline_ensemble.py from the files.
admissibility_gate.on_failure: A member that fails is reported and the ensemble gives no verdict; it is never replaced by a tuned or substitute timeline, and the gate is never changed after a result.

results_at_registration.T1: passes G1-G5 (recorded baseline 20261028T135241Z: valid, reruns identical; rebuilt on 2026-10-29 outside the repository with the generalised build: same network, program and demand hashes, and identical tripinfo on all 20 seeds)
results_at_registration.T2: passes G1-G5 (recorded baseline 20261028T141919Z; rebuilt likewise with identical hashes and tripinfo)
results_at_registration.T3: passes G1-G4: G1 and G4 and the timeline parts of G2 and G3 in signal_estimate_v2a.json; the compiled parts on a throwaway compile (0 priority conflicts, 0 seconds where the replay program differs from the timeline). G5 not yet run: no baseline was built before this design was committed

cross_timeline_rule.per_member: Each member is an ordinary replay experiment evaluated on its own under rules 0.3.0: paired 95% t intervals over seeds 1-20, uncorrected worsening, Holm's correction over that member's own planned family (3 candidates x the improvement metrics), entry blocking, and uninformative maximum queues. Per-member eligibility is read from cairoflow_evaluation.report.candidate_standings, not reimplemented.
cross_timeline_rule.supported_on_a_member: All of: (1) the structural precondition holds there; (2) every comparison of the candidate has exactly the planned paired seeds 1-20, and it has a comparison for every metric the baseline measured; (3) its standing is eligible: compared on every seed, no metric worsens, no more vehicles held off the network at any entry than the baseline, at least one Holm-confirmed improvement.
cross_timeline_rule.robust_improvement: Supported on every required member (T1-T4). The improvements it claims are those confirmed on every required member; if none is common to all, that is stated.
cross_timeline_rule.timeline_dependent: Supported on some required members but not all; the record gives the per-member table (status, worsened metrics, confirmed improvements, entry blocking, mean-delay difference and interval, phase mapping) and why it fails on each.
cross_timeline_rule.robust_harm: A metric that worsens on every required member.
cross_timeline_rule.direction_disagreements: Every metric whose verdict is not the same on every member, with each member's verdict, mean difference and interval; flagged opposite when one member says improves and another worsens.
cross_timeline_rule.multiplicity: Holm's family stays per member, as fixed by each experiment. Requiring confirmation on every required member is an intersection-union test, so a false robust claim is no more likely than one member's family-wise 5%; no further correction is applied.
cross_timeline_rule.never: Values are never pooled, averaged or weighted across members, and no member is dropped or down-weighted after its result is seen.
cross_timeline_rule.selection: Among robust improvements: most Holm-confirmed improvements on the candidate's worst member, then the smallest worst-member mean-delay difference, then the lower intervention number.
cross_timeline_rule.recommendation: A robust selection is a recommendation only when every required member's baseline is assessed as validated. None is (T1 and T2 partially validated; T3 and T4 not assessed), so nothing can be recommended under this design.

structural_precondition.rule: A candidate is the same plan on a member only if each of its phase changes (a cut-cycle phase, mapped onto the replay by phase identity) applies to at least one replayed phase there. A change that applies to 0 phases means the candidate is not the same plan on that member, so it cannot be supported there and cannot be robust. The applied, clamped and already-shorter counts are read from the candidate networks' notes and recorded per member.
structural_precondition.found_from_mapping_alone: Computed on 2026-10-29 by compiling each member's replay program and mapping the three validated outcomes onto it, with no simulation. I1 (west -6 s, north/south through +9 s) and I2 (north/south through -5 s, protected lefts +5 s) apply on all four members; I1's west change applies to 14, 15, 15 and 14 phases on T1-T4, of which 3, 1, 2 and 2 stop at the 5 s minimum. I3's north-only +4 s applies to 9 phases on T1 and T3 but to 0 on T2 and T4 (every such phase is already shorter than 5 s), so I3 fails the precondition on T2 and T4 and cannot be a robust improvement.

already_known_when_written: The candidates' results on T1 (experiments/records/ngsim-int2-realism-experiment-20261028T135556Z.json, rules 0.2.0) and on T2 (ngsim-int2-realism-experiment-20261028T142330Z.json) were known: on T1 every candidate worsens mean delay (I1 +5.40 s, I2 +3.29 s, I3 +3.74 s) and none is selected; on T2 I1 improves mean delay (-0.75 s, Holm-confirmed) but worsens throughput and the west and east queues, I2 and I3 worsen delay, and none is selected.
The I3 mapping finding above was known from the structure alone (on T2 it was also in the recorded experiment's notes).
The new members' timeline-level statistics (west green, all-red seconds, crossings shown red) were computed before this design was written; no baseline or candidate run on T3 or T4 had been made.

Rules 0.3.0 (ADR-024: uninformative maximum queues, entry blocking) were committed (bb87450) while this design was written, before any member was evaluated under them; every member is evaluated under them, T1 and T2 included, so T1 and T2 are re-evaluated rather than read from their rules 0.2.0 records.

A smoke test of the ensemble runner read the existing T1 and T2 experiments (rules 0.2.0) with the rules check bypassed; it reproduced the already-known results (no candidate eligible on either) and is not a result of this ensemble.

excluded_variants.variant: start-up lost time 1 s or 3 s (instead of 2 s)
excluded_variants.evidence: All 19 lead vehicles waiting at an estimated onset pass 2 m/s 0.5-5.1 s after it (median 2.4 s); none moves before it (scenario.json onset_check).
excluded_variants.reason: 1 s would put the west lead vehicle's departure (0.5 s) before its green. Either value shifts every onset by 1 s, which moves the known window to [119, 752) or [117, 750): other observed vehicles would be replayed, and the cut at 564 s no longer compiles.

excluded_variants.evidence: No gap between consecutive reference crossings on any head falls in [22.1, 32.5) s; 30 s gives byte-identical timelines.
excluded_variants.reason: Fixed by the data. Below 22.1 s the west lull at 408-430 s (its own green, no conflicting green) would be split; above 32.5 s windows merge across real phase changes.

excluded_variants.evidence: It turns lone crossings (south through at 531.4 s, north left at 688.1 s, west at 218.9 s on version 1) into 5 s greens.
excluded_variants.reason: A lone crossing is not evidence of a phase; doing so lowers agreement elsewhere (south left 0.60 to 0.53, south through 0.992 to 0.984 in green or yellow).

excluded_variants.variant: yellow 4 s, all-red 1 s, minimum green 5 s changed
excluded_variants.evidence: Synthetic constants; the trajectories carry no evidence for them.
excluded_variants.reason: Not propagated. The yellow-placement axis already brackets where the last crossing sits within green and yellow. East greens are 5 s clamps, i.e. lower bounds; a longer value would be unobserved.

excluded_variants.variant: fill red gaps up to the next conflicting onset (an upper bound on greens)
excluded_variants.evidence: All heads show red for 111, 84, 83 and 49 s of the window on T1-T4.
excluded_variants.reason: Rejected by ADR-023: it invents green time in which nobody crossed.

excluded_variants.variant: other head structures (a protected west left, the south left not following the north left, the east following the west)
excluded_variants.evidence: North left: 5% of lefts during the opposing through (threshold 20%); south left: 67% in the north left's service (threshold 50%); east: 0% in the west's service; a west protected left cannot be tested (8 east throughs, fewer than 20).
excluded_variants.reason: Each decision clears its threshold with margin or cannot be tested; a different head set would also change phase signatures, so the candidates would map onto different phases (other plans).

excluded_variants.variant: trim the later window instead of the earlier one at a conflict
excluded_variants.evidence: Onsets are the best-evidenced point (19 of 19 confirmed by lead-vehicle departures); green ends are the weakest.
excluded_variants.reason: The existing order keeps the better evidence.

excluded_variants.variant: rules tuned until the paired crossing lags are smallest
excluded_variants.evidence: The lags are measured on the same crossings the timeline is estimated from.
excluded_variants.reason: Rejected by ADR-023: it would fit the noise.

excluded_variants.variant: a bootstrap of the estimate (resampled crossings)
excluded_variants.reason: Deferred: a different method, not a choice among rules; it would need its own design.

assumptions: The two SignalRevision axes are the estimation choices the evidence leaves open; the others are fixed by the data or are synthetic constants this design does not propagate.

The candidates are carried onto each member by phase identity; where a change applies to fewer phases, or is clamped at the minimum green, the plan differs between members, and the per-member mapping is recorded.
Every member replays one observed 10.5 minute realisation; the 20 seeds measure SUMO's microscopic noise, not demand uncertainty.
Cross-street entries are anchored to each member's own greens, so cross-street demand timing differs between members by construction.
limitations: The ensemble brackets two rule choices; it is not a probability distribution over timelines, and a robust verdict is not a calibrated probability.

Synthetic constants (yellow, all-red, minimum green, start-up lost time), east greens that are lower bounds, red gaps, the window edges, south over-stopping and right turners' stops remain unpropagated.
West and east results are not trusted on their own (ADR-022), and mean delay has no observed counterpart.
No member's baseline is assessed as validated, so nothing found under this design is a recommendation.
The agreement of any timeline with the crossings is internal consistency: the timelines are estimated from the same crossings.
